tools.name: list_tables
tools.description: Find tables in the library. Each result gives its slug, the question it answers, its size and when it was last read.

tools.name: get_table
tools.description: Read a table: its scope, its columns with the rule for each, a summary of what each column holds, and its rows. A null value is blank. `origins` says where a row's unquoted values came from, `ai` says how far each AI column has got, and `versions` lists saved versions. For a big table, read the summ

tools.name: get_cell
tools.description: The evidence for one value: the source, the exact quote, what kind of source it is and when it was read. For a missing value, where we looked, and `absent` means the source was read and gives no such value. `url` is the cell's lasting address, showing its proof, for citing. `confirmed` says how a se

tools.name: check_claim
tools.description: Test a statement against one cell, such as whether a value in a draft or an answer is right. The verdict is `matches`, `differs` (with what the source states), `disputed` (sources disagree, see `conflicts`) or `unknown` (no acceptable source stated it, so say so). It compares values and doesn't judg

tools.name: export_table
tools.description: A table as CSV, ready to save as a file or load into a notebook. The first column is each row's name unless `names` is false. `columns` picks columns by id, in that order. With `proof`, each column is followed by its source and quote, and in a table whose proof is optional, by where each value came

tools.name: propose_change
tools.description: Suggest a new value for a cell, with its proof. The quote must be word for word from the source and state the value. The owner reviews it before anything changes. Needs a token sent as a Bearer token.

tools.name: create_table
tools.description: Make a private draft table, ready to fill, for anything from a tracker to a dataset. Its values say where they came from unless you set `proof` to `required`. Only `title`, `columns` and `rows` are needed now, but give `question`, `scope`, and a `rule` for each column if you can: a person has to sup

tools.name: add_columns
tools.description: Add columns to a draft you run, such as a blank one a person started. Returns the new column ids for fill_cells. Needs a token.

tools.name: add_rows
tools.description: Add up to 500 rows to a table you run. Each row is a name, or an object with its `values` by column id or label, so a whole tracker or dataset goes in a few calls. A row without a `key` gets the next free number. A name the table already has gets the values given for it, so syncing again from the sa

tools.name: fill_cells
tools.description: Set up to 200 cells of a table you run. Usually a cell gives `value` and `origin` (`entered`, `imported` with a `note` like the file or email it came from, `link` with its `source`, or `generated`). Left out, the origin is `link` when there's a `source` and `generated` when there isn't. These can go

tools.name: data_link
tools.description: A private address that loads a table you run as CSV, for a notebook, a script or a spreadsheet, with the lines to do it. Add `?columns=a,b` to pick columns and `?names=0` to leave out row names. Anyone with the link can read the data, and `fresh` makes a new one so the old one stops working. Needs a

tools.name: save_version
tools.description: Freeze a table you run as it stands now, as a numbered version with a lasting link that never changes. Do this before training on a dataset or citing a table, and name the version you used. Needs a token.

tools.name: fork_table
tools.description: Copy a table into your own account as a private draft, to extend or relabel: any published public table, or one you run. Every value keeps its proof or origin, and the copy remembers where it came from. Needs a token.

tools.name: set_instruction
tools.description: Make a column an AI column, change its instruction, or turn it back into a plain column with an empty one. The instruction says what to work out for each row and names other columns in braces, like "Classify {Pitch} by genre". Its values never overwrite what a person typed, linked or quoted. Needs p

tools.name: next_ai_cells
tools.description: The next prompts to answer for a table's AI columns, up to 200 at a time: blank cells first, then answers whose row or instruction has changed. Answer each prompt yourself, then send the answers back with fill_ai_cells, each with its `row` and `basis`. Repeat until it says `done`. `redo` also re-ans

tools.name: fill_ai_cells
tools.description: Save up to 200 answers to an AI column, each with the `row` and `basis` next_ai_cells gave it. An answer outside the column's choices, or to a prompt that has since changed, comes back with a reason. Each value is saved as generated, with the instruction and `model`. Needs a token.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "propose_change" references sensitive artifacts (bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_cell, fill_cells · Private data: export_table, propose_change, create_table, add_columns, add_rows, fill_cells, data_link, save_version, fork_table, set_instruction, next_ai_cells, fill_ai_cells · Public sink: add_rows, fill_cells, next_ai_cells · Destructive: add_columns, add_rows, fill_cells, data_link, save_version, fork_table, set_instruction.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_cell, fill_cells · Private data: export_table, propose_change, create_table, add_columns, add_rows, fill_cells, data_link, save_version, fork_table, set_instruction, next_ai_cells, fill_ai_cells · Public sink: add_rows, fill_cells, next_ai_cells · Destructive: add_columns, add_rows, fill_cells, data_link, save_version, fork_table, set_instruction

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
